Key.Original: Seconds between object-temperature scans. Surface temperatures change on time constants of 600 seconds and longer, so a scan every tick is wasted work. 0 scans every tick.

Key.Original: Thermal selections repainted per second. The engine re-uploads a procedural texture for each one, and that cost lands on the render thread where no script timer sees it. The physics still solves every pass, so the image gain and every thermal coupling are unaffected.

Key.Original: The host channel for the thermal display. Vanilla TI runs the display on the engine's own thermal channel overlaid on the vehicle's native TI. DTV disables the vehicle's native TI and draws the display over the day channel instead, the route the proven A3TI and MKK thermal mods use, so the engine's TI pass cannot fight the mod's. DTV is vehicle-only: the player must be in a vehicle optic. It is a prototype for comparison and is the only channel that does not set the ppEffectForceInNVG flag.
Key.English: The host channel for the thermal display. Vanilla TI runs the display on the engine's own thermal channel overlaid on the vehicle's native TI. DTV disables the vehicle's native TI and draws the display over the day channel instead, the route the proven A3TI and MKK thermal mods use, so the engine's TI pass cannot fight the mod's. DTV is vehicle-only: the player must be in a vehicle optic. It is a prototype for comparison and is the only channel that does not set the ppEffectForceInNVG flag.

Key.English: Thermal Diagnostics

Key.Original: Automatic follows the scene radiance histogram (AGC). Manual uses the fixed window below, like the level and span control on a real thermography or thermal weapon sight. Local normalises each object to its own selection range: it widens that object's internal contrast, but it breaks comparison between objects because a hot and a cold object can map to the same ramp. The local gain is capped at 8 times, so a flat object is not given invented contrast.
Key.English: Automatic follows the scene radiance histogram (AGC). Manual uses the fixed window below, like the level and span control on a real thermography or thermal weapon sight. Local normalises each object to its own selection range: it widens that object's internal contrast, but it breaks comparison between objects because a hot and a cold object can map to the same ramp. The local gain is capped at 8 times, so a flat object is not given invented contrast.

Applies the full-screen thermal effects: colour grade, black-hot inversion, sensor grain, IR-scatter blur, the ocular vignette, the rain lens film and the sensor pixelation. Turn OFF to isolate their render cost.
Thermal Post-Process Effects

Key.Original: Ember interpolates the engine's own decoded thermal colours through a continuous ramp. White hot grey is the luminance form of the same ramp. The isotherm modes are the MKK thermal highlight colours as procedural two-tone ramps: a body below the display window midpoint stays cold, a body at or above it takes the mode hue (red, green, yellow, magenta or sepia).
Key.English: Ember interpolates the engine's own decoded thermal colours through a continuous ramp. White hot grey is the luminance form of the same ramp. The isotherm modes are the MKK thermal highlight colours as procedural two-tone ramps: a body below the display window midpoint stays cold, a body at or above it takes the mode hue (red, green, yellow, magenta or sepia).

Key.Original: Quantise the thermal display to the fitted device's vertical detector resolution, so a low-resolution sensor shows the blocks its detector actually resolves. A sensor finer than the render shows none. The figure is the device's own; the engine clamps it.
